prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1444; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured reports vehicle front bumper and hood damage. Claimant vehicle reported with front-end damage. Claimant reports neck and back strain and was transported to urgent care. Liability appears disputed pending police report review.

Entry 2: Police report received. Officer notes both vehicles were traveling at low speed when they made contact. Insured's statement and claimant's statement differ on which vehicle crossed the center line. Scene photos requested from insured for file.

Entry 3: Claimant is now represented by counsel. All further communication to go through the attorney's office. Letter of representation received and logged. Request for medical records and treatment history sent to counsel.

Entry 4: Medical records received from urgent care and primary physician. Diagnosis consistent with cervical and lumbar strain. Treatment includes physical therapy and muscle relaxants. Records reviewed and flagged for independent medical review given ongoing treatment.

Entry 5: Counsel contacted to confirm receipt of medical file and request a settlement position. Claim remains open pending independent medical review, repair estimate finalization, and liability determination. Supervisor notified of representation and reserve review scheduled.
